title: JMC Racing
subtitle: Business origin, BMX entry, prototypes and production are documented as separate phases.
summary: JMC Racing's public history is strongest when its phases remain separate: a bicycle business established in 1969, direct BMX involvement around 1974, a shop team in 1975, XP prototype development in 1976 and production-frame launches in March and April 1977. Model and serial conclusions remain tied to period, construction and company records.

claims.statement: JMC began producing BMX frames in 1969.
claims.public_wording: The business that became JMC was established in 1969; BMX involvement developed in the mid-1970s and production frames began in 1977.
claims.evidence_summary: JMC's history separates business origin, BMX involvement, prototype development and production-frame launch.
claims.does_not_prove: The 1969 business date is not a BMX frame-production date.

claims.statement: JMC1 and JMC20 were the first production short and long frames.
claims.public_wording: JMC's archive identifies JMC1 and JMC20 as its first production short and long frames, dated March and April 1977.
claims.evidence_summary: The company identification guide preserves the serials, dates and short/long roles.
claims.does_not_prove: Any present-day claimant frame still requires serial, construction, provenance and certification evidence.

claims.statement: The first two digits of every JMC serial identify the production year.
claims.public_wording: JMC serial interpretation depends on model, period, prefix and construction features; the first two digits are not a universal year code.
claims.evidence_summary: Early frames used sequential JMC numbers, model prefixes appeared later and the public archive describes a transition rather than a universal rule.

timeline.event: The bicycle business later associated with JMC was established.
JM Cyclery organized a BMX shop team that included Harry Leary.
XP prototype development included short and long configurations.
JMC1 and JMC20 are identified as the first production short and long frames.
